newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen steady-up $0.50-trade.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen steady-up $0.50-trade.

text.p: Midwest direct cash hog prices Thursday were seen steady to $0.50 per cwt higher, lifted by continued strong packer demand and ideas that producers were becoming current in their marketings, livestock dealers said.
Top prices for hogs delivered to plants in Iowa and southern Minnesota were expected to range from $52.50 to $53.50, up $0.50 from Wednesday.
Illinois top hog prices at plants were seen ranging from $51.50 to $52.00 and Indiana/Ohio top plant prices could range from $51.00 to $52.00, dealers said.
Cash hog prices also were supported by active packer buying on firm pork demand and improved operating margins, they said.

Carlot pork prices at midday were mixed, with fresh loins unevenly steady and lightweight hams $1.00 to $2.00 per cwt higher, USDA said. There were 67.75 loads of pork cuts and 28.0 loads of trimmings sold, according to USDA.

Talk that hog supplies were starting to decline as farmers finish selling hogs that were held back by harvesting, lent further support. Prices also were underpinned by talk that packers were planning a large Saturday slaughter, they said.
